detailed_results.issue: I notice that people I assigned the test in October of 2025 have not received new tests. How long do the tests stay active in the system.
detailed_results.subject: Test Active in the system
detailed_results.expected_response:
Hi,


Tests in HackerRank remain active indefinitely unless a start and end time are set. 
Without these, tests do not expire automatically.



To set expiration times, specify a start and end date/time in the test settings. After expiration:

Invited candidates cannot access the test.
The "Invite" button is disabled; no new invitations can be sent.


To check or change expiration settings:

Go to the test's Settings and select the General section.
Update the Start date & time and End date & time fields as needed.
To keep the test active indefinitely, clear these fields by clicking the clear icon (X).


If the test has an expiration set, adjust these settings to enable new invitations.
detailed_results.predicted_response:
Overview

In HackerRank, the duration a test invitation remains active is determined by the expiry settings configured during the invitation process. By default, invitations are set to 'Never' expire, meaning they remain active indefinitely unless manually modified.

Steps to Check or Modify Expiry

1. Navigate to the specific test invitation settings.
2. Locate the 'Expiry' dropdown menu.
3. Review the current setting. If a specific date was selected, the invitation will expire at that time.
4. If you wish to change this, you can select 'Custom' to define a new expiry date, time, and time zone, or set it to 'Never' to keep the invitation active.

Notes

- Once a test invitation expires, candidates can no longer access the test, and the 'Invite' button for that specific instance is disabled.
- If you are using an integration (such as Greenhouse), ensure the test itself is active and not expired, as this will prevent the system from sending new tests.

Reference

https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/6027855406-inviting-candidates-to-a-test

Restoring an archived test

To restore an archived test: 

1. Open the test you want to restore.

2. Click the more options menu (⋮) in the top right corner.

3. Select **Restore**.

4. In the confirmation dialog, click **Restore** to confirm. A success message appears.

Once restored:

- The test moves back to your list of Active Tests.

- Candidate invites are re-enabled.

**Note: **

- You can also restore the test by clicking the **Restore Test** button at the top of the test page.

- You can archive or restore multiple tests at once.

 - In the **Active Tests** tab, select the checkboxes next to the tests you want to archive, and click **Archive**.

 - In the **Archived Tests** tab, select the checkboxes next to the tests you want to restore, and click **Restore**.

Set an expiry date

You can define how long a test invitation remains active. After the expiry time, the test invitation expires, and candidate(s) can no longer take the Test. 

To set the expiration date: 

1. Click the **Expiry** dropdown.

2. Select an expiry option from the list.

 - If you choose **Custom**, select the expiry date, time, and time zone, and then click **Save.**

The selected expiry date appears.

**Note:** By default, the **Expiry** option is set to **Never**, and the invitation does not expire.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**Why is the Greenhouse Integration page not showing in my HackerRank account?**

You do not have admin access to your HackerRank account. Only admins can access the integration settings page.

**Why don’t I see the ATS Settings updated message after I click Test and Save?**

Verify that you entered the correct Greenhouse User ID and Harvest API Token in HackerRank.

**Why am I the only user who can’t send tests through Greenhouse?**

 Check the following:

- Your HackerRank and Greenhouse login email addresses match.

- You have a Recruiter or Company Admin access in HackerRank.

- You have **Send Test** permissions in HackerRank.

- The test you are trying to send is active (not expired or deleted).

Modify Test Expiration Time Prerequisite Modifying test expiration time

You can define a start and end time (including time zone) to control when a test remains active.

Candidates can attempt the test only during the active period. After the test expires:

- Invited candidates cannot access the test.

- The **Invite** button is disabled.

- You cannot invite new candidates.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**Does the AI-Assisted Summary work in proctored tests?**

Yes. In proctored tests, the **Performance Summary** appears in the new reports interface.

**Can I view the AI Fluency in older reports?**

In the classic reports view, the AI Fluency is available only at the question level, but not at the test level.

**Is the AI Fluency reliable?**

Refer to the [📄 AI Fluency](/articles/1773201418)article.

**When should I use the Unguarded AI Assistant?**

You can use the Unguarded AI Assistant when you want to evaluate how candidates work with AI in real-world, agent-style workflows.

I'm noticing that you all have many default versions of roles. (e.g. front end developer for react, angular, vue.js, etc.) What do you consider best practice 
for when to create a new test versus create a variant of the test? What are the advantages and disadvantages of using variants?
detailed_results.subject:
When should I create a variant versus
 have a different test?
detailed_results.expected_response:
Hi,


Consider these guidelines when choosing between creating a new test or a variant:



When to Use Test Variants:

Create variants to adapt a single test to different candidate profiles, 
such as roles with different tech stacks (React, Angular, Vue.js).
Variants streamline assessments by showing candidates only relevant sections and generating role-specific reports.


Advantages of Test Variants:

Reduces the need to manage multiple tests, improving efficiency.
Decreases maintenance while allowing scalable personalization.
Ensures candidates are tested on relevant content.


Disadvantages and Limitations of Test Variants:

A test must have at least two variants to function; you cannot delete a variant if only two exist.
Variants without logic are hidden from candidates until logic is added.
detailed_results.predicted_response:
### Overview

Test variants are designed to streamline assessments for roles that require different tech stacks (e.g., Node.js, Python, or Java) within a single, unified test setup. 

### When to Use Variants

Use variants when you want to assess candidates for the same role but need to offer different technical paths. By using variants, you can deliver the correct version based on a candidate's input at login. This approach keeps your reporting clean, as insights are specific to the variant attempted, and it reduces maintenance overhead compared to managing multiple independent tests.

### Advantages of Variants

- **Streamlined Management:** Consolidates multiple tech-stack assessments into one test.
- **Personalized Assessment:** Candidates only see sections relevant to their specific skills.
- **Clean Reporting:** Insights are segmented by the specific variant attempted.
- **Efficiency:** You can reuse sections across variants or add skill-based questions to specific versions.

### How to Create Variants

1. Log in to your **HackerRank for Work** account.
2. Navigate to the **Tests** tab and open the desired test.
3. Go to the **Questions** tab.
4. Click the more option menu (**⋮**) and select **Create Variants**.
5. Use the **+** icon to add additional variants as needed.

For more details, please refer to the official documentation: https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/7530103378-test-variants

Creating test variants

To create test variants:

1. Log in to your **HackerRank for Work** account using your credentials.

2. Go to the **Tests** tab.

3. Open the test you want to modify.

4. Go to the **Questions** tab.

5. Click the more option menu (**⋮**) in the top right corner.

6. Select **Create Variants.**

7. Click **Create Variants.**

The system converts the existing test into **Variant 1** and opens **Variant 2**, where you can start creating the second version. To add more variants, select the **+** icon next to the tabs.

**Note:** A variant-based test requires at least two variants.

**Test Variants **

You can now create multiple variations of a test and deliver the correct one based on the candidate's input at login. This makes it easy to assess candidates working with different tech stacks—like Node.js, Python, or Java, using a single, streamlined test setup.

Candidates see only the sections relevant to them, and reports reflect just the variant they attempted, so insights stay clean, role-specific, and easy to evaluate. This reduces maintenance overhead while giving you the flexibility to personalize assessments at scale.

For more information, see [📄 Test Variants](/articles/7530103378).

Adding questions or sections to a variant

To add questions or sections:

1. Select the variant tab (for example, Variant 2).

2. Click **Add New**.

3. Choose one of the following options:

 - **Add Skill-Based Questions**: Use HackerRank-curated questions grouped by skill.

 - **Add Manually**: Select questions from the library or create custom questions.

 - **Add from Other Variants**: Reuse existing sections from other test variants.

4. Select the relevant questions or sections.

5. Click **Add** to include them in the variant.

**Note:** You can also add skill-based questions or reuse existing sections directly from the empty variant screen using the **Add New Skill Bundle** or **Add from Other Variants** buttons.

Test Variant Updates

### Test Variant Overview

When you create a variant of an existing test, you now see a clear overview that explains how test variants work. This helps you get oriented before setup, whether you are new to variants or need a quick refresher.

### Add Time to Candidate Attempts

You can now grant time accommodations to candidates taking variant-based tests. Time adjustments can be applied at the section level for each candidate.

For bulk updates, select multiple candidates from the same test variant. The relevant test sections will be displayed, allowing you to add time where applicable.

Time adjustments can only be applied when all selected candidates belong to the same variant. If candidates from different variants are selected, the Add time option is disabled and you’ll be prompted to filter your selection to a single variant before proceeding.

### Simplified Test Variant Logic Creation

Creating test variant criteria is now more intuitive. The redesigned Add Variant Logic workflow lets you route candidates to different test variants based on their answers to a qualifying question.

Subscription plans

**What happens if I exceed my new plan’s limits during a downgrade transition?**

You continue to have access to your current plan features and credits (Entitlements included in your subscription) until the cycle ends, even if your usage exceeds the new plan’s limits.

**Do I get a refund when I upgrade mid-cycle?**

No. You pay the prorated difference for the upgrade and gain immediate access to new features.

**Can I change from monthly to quarterly billing without changing my plan tier?**

Yes. HackerRank treats this as an upgrade. The change takes effect immediately with prorated billing.

**What happens to my unused credits when I upgrade?**

HackerRank forfeits all unused credits from your previous plan. You immediately receive the full credit allocation of your new plan.

**What should I do if I accidentally click Start Test and lose a credit?**

When you click **Start Test**, the system immediately records your attempt. However, you do not lose access to the test. You can return and continue from where you left off at any time.

If your Visa Traveller's Cheques have been stolen, you must contact the issuing bank immediately to report the loss and initiate a refund process. Since your cheques were issued by Citicorp, please contact them directly to report the theft.

#### Steps to Request a Refund

1. **Contact the Issuer:** Reach out to Citicorp to report the theft.
2. **Prepare Required Information:** The issuer will require the following details to process your request:
   - Cheque serial numbers.
   - Location and date of purchase.
   - Details regarding how and when the cheques were lost or stolen.
   - Confirmation of the issuer (Citicorp).

Refunds can typically be arranged within 24 hours, subject to the issuer's terms and conditions.
